title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck is setting up the Shimura–Taniyama main theorem of complex multiplication in the adelic, 'Deligne-style' form, as notes for himself or a student. The setting is a CM field K, a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real F with g = [F:Q]. The objects are triples (A, m, α):
(a) A, an abelian variety up to isogeny over Q̄ of dimension g;
(b) m, an action of K on A;
(c) α = (α_ℓ), for each ℓ an isomorphism of K⊗Q_ℓ-modules K⊗Q_ℓ ≅ V_ℓ(A).
The datum (c) amounts to a level structure trivialising the finite adelic Tate module as a free rank-one module over the finite adeles of K; the integrality for almost all ℓ is made explicit on the next page.

The problem is to describe how Gal(Q̄/Q) permutes isomorphism classes of such triples. He admits this is only partly possible: 'On n'y arrive pas tout à fait.'

The construction proceeds as follows.
- K⊗Q̄ ≅ Q̄^{Hom(K,Q̄)}, so Lie(A) is a K⊗Q̄-module, i.e. a representation over Q̄ of the torus K* = R_{K/Q}(G_m). Its weights form the CM type Φ, a subset of Hom(K,Q̄).
- Its determinant ∧^g Lie(A) gives the character det Lie = ∏_{φ∈Φ} φ : K* → G_m.
- The 'corps dual' K' is the field of definition of this character, i.e. the reflex field of (K,Φ).
- Equivalently, K' is the smallest subfield of Q̄ over which the K–Q̄ bimodule Lie A descends to a K–K' bimodule L_0, with Lie A ≅ L_0 ⊗_{K'} Q̄.
- L_0 yields a morphism of Q-tori δ : K'* → K*, k' ↦ det_K(k' | L_0). This is the reflex norm N_Φ'.
- δ induces a map on idele classes from K' to K.

The next page states the theorem. For u ∈ Gal(Q̄/K') with idele ũ attached by class field theory, u(A,m,α) ≅ (A, m, δ(ũ)^{-1}∘α). This uses the fact that δ kills Ker(N : F'* → G_m), so the finite part of δ(ũ) mod K* is well defined. The CM elliptic curve case follows as an example.
errors: No genuine error. Condition (c) as written ('for each ℓ an isomorphism') omits the requirement that the α_ℓ be integral for almost all ℓ, i.e. that they assemble into an isomorphism of finite adelic modules; the next page supplies this.
Calling K* 'le groupe algébrique' and det Lie 'défini sur Q̄' is fine. δ is defined over Q because L_0 is a K⊗K'-module.

Historical remark: 'on n'y arrive pas tout à fait', i.e. only Gal(Q̄/K') is described. This was the state of the classical theorem. Langlands (1979) had conjectured the full Gal(Q̄/Q) / Aut(C) description, and Tate and Deligne proved it around 1981 (Tate's 'Taniyama group' and conjugation of CM abelian varieties; Deligne in LNM 900). Grothendieck seems unaware of, or ignoring, this simultaneous development.

ideas.what: Adelic triples (A up to isogeny, K-action, trivialisation of V_ℓ as K⊗Q_ℓ-module) as the objects on which Galois acts
ideas.modern_name: CM abelian varieties with level structure / points of a zero-dimensional Shimura variety for the torus K*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama (1961); adelic reformulation Deligne (Variétés de Shimura, 1971/1979), Milne

ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama; this characterisation is standard in Deligne/Milne

ideas.what: δ : K'* → K*, k' ↦ det_K(k' on L_0), and induced map on idele classes

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, standard (Deligne/Milne-style) formulation of the main theorem of CM, with the reflex field and reflex norm defined via the determinant of Lie A. All of it is textbook material. The only mild interest is historical: Grothendieck in 1981 calls the full Gal(Q̄/Q) action out of reach just as Tate and Deligne were settling Langlands' conjecture, and he says he wishes motives were mentioned more.
transcription_corrections: In (c) the arrow K⊗Q_ℓ → T_ℓ(A)⊗Q_ℓ appears to carry the label α_ℓ (written above the arrow), not just '~'. Above T_ℓ(A)⊗Q_ℓ is written 'V_ℓ(A) ='.
Page number written at bottom is 122.
